title: Step 1b - Applying ReLU to Convolutional Layers: Breaking Up Image Linearity

cues.en: -: Hello and welcome back to the course on deep learning.
cues.zh: 大家好，歡迎回到深度學習課程。

cues.en: Today we're talking about ReLU, which is rectified linear units.
cues.zh: 今天談 ReLU，也就是修正線性單元。

cues.en: And this is an additional step on top of our convolution step.
cues.zh: 這是在卷積步驟之上加的一個步驟。

cues.en: So it's not a separate big step, it's a small step.
cues.zh: 它不是獨立的大步驟，而是小步驟，

cues.en: It's step 1 B basically.
cues.zh: 基本上就是第 1 步的 B 部分。

cues.en: And what is going on here?
cues.zh: 這裡會發生什麼事？

cues.en: Well, we have our input image, we have our convolution layer, which we've discussed, and then on top of that, we're going to apply, wait for it,
cues.zh: 先有輸入影像和前面介紹過的卷積層，接著還要套用，準備好了嗎，

cues.en: our favorite rectifier function, and you're really familiar with the rectifier function from the previous section on artificial neural networks.
cues.zh: 我們最喜歡的整流函數。上一章人工神經網路已經介紹過，你應該很熟悉。

cues.en: So sometimes authors or instructors separate the convolution and the rectifier as to separate steps.
cues.zh: 有些作者或講師會把卷積和整流函數分成兩個步驟。

cues.en: In our examples, we are just going to consider them just one big step for second convolution, then the rectifier.
cues.zh: 我們的例子則把它們視為一個大步驟，先卷積，再套用整流函數。

cues.en: And the reason why we're applying the rectifier is because we want to increase non-linearity in our image or in our network, in our commercial neural network.
cues.zh: 使用整流函數，是為了增加影像或網路，也就是卷積神經網路的非線性。

cues.en: And rectifier acts as that filter or acts as that function which breaks up linearity.
cues.zh: 整流函數就像濾波器，或一個打破線性的函數。

cues.en: And the reason why we want to increase non-linearity in our network is because images themselves are highly non-linear, especially if you're recognizing different objects
cues.zh: 我們希望提高網路的非線性，是因為影像本身高度非線性，特別是辨識相鄰的不同物體，

cues.en: next to each other or just on just backgrounds and stuff like that, like, the image is going to have lots of non-linear elements, and the transition between pixels, adjacent pixels is often gonna be non-linear.
cues.zh: 或各種背景上的物體時。影像包含很多非線性元素，相鄰像素之間的變化也經常是非線性的。

cues.en: That's, you know, because there's borders, there's different colors, there's different elements in your images.
cues.zh: 因為影像裡有邊界、不同顏色及不同元素。

cues.en: But at the same time, when we're applying mathematical operations such as convolution and running this feature detection to create our feature maps,
cues.zh: 但套用卷積這類數學運算，透過特徵偵測建立特徵圖時，

cues.en: we risk that we might create something linear, and therefore, we need to break up the linearity.
cues.zh: 有可能產生線性的結果，因此需要打破這種線性。

cues.en: So let's have a look at an example.
cues.zh: 來看個例子。

cues.en: Here is a image, an original image.
cues.zh: 這是一張原始影像。

cues.en: Now, when we apply a feature detector to this image, we get something like this.
cues.zh: 對它套用特徵偵測器，就會得到這樣的結果。

cues.en: So you can see here that black is negative, white is positive values.
cues.zh: 這裡黑色代表負值，白色代表正值。

cues.en: Well, when you apply a feature detector to, like, a proper image, which has not just zeros and ones but has lots of different values, and you apply,
cues.zh: 對真正的影像套用特徵偵測器時，影像不只有 0 和 1，而有許多不同數值；

cues.en: as we saw previously, feature detects can have negative values in themselves, sometimes you'll get negative values.
cues.zh: 先前也看過，特徵偵測器本身可能有負值，所以結果有時會出現負值。

cues.en: And here or there black ones are negative, white ones are positive.
cues.zh: 這裡的黑色是負值，白色是正值。

cues.en: And what a rectified linear unit function does is it removes all the black, right?
cues.zh: 修正線性單元函數會把所有黑色部分去除。

cues.en: Anything below zero turns into zero.
cues.zh: 任何小於 0 的值都變成 0。

cues.en: And so from this, it turns into this, right?
cues.zh: 所以從這樣變成這樣。

cues.en: And so it's pretty hard to see what exactly is the benefit
cues.zh: 不過很難直接看出這對

cues.en: in terms of breaking up linearity.
cues.zh: 打破線性有什麼幫助。

cues.en: I'll try to explain, I'll try to, like, show an example on this image, but at the end of the day, this is a very mathematical concept, and we'd have to go
cues.zh: 我試著用這張影像舉例解釋，但這終究是很數學性的概念，必須深入

cues.en: into a lot of math to really explain what is going on.
cues.zh: 許多數學內容，才能完整說明。

cues.en: But let's try, let's have a look.
cues.zh: 不過還是來試著看看。

cues.en: So for instance, let's look at this building here, right?
cues.zh: 例如看看這棟建築。

cues.en: So this is a building on its own.
cues.zh: 這是一棟獨立的建築。

cues.en: Then, you can see this shadow, this black part, this shadow over here.
cues.zh: 這裡可以看到陰影，也就是這塊黑色部分。

cues.en: Well, you can see that it's white, the reflection of the light, and then it's a gray, and then it gets darker, and then it gets darker again, right?
cues.zh: 反光的地方是白色，接著是灰色，然後越來越暗、再更暗。

cues.en: And when we take it out, we take out that black part.
cues.zh: 我們去除的就是這塊黑色部分。

cues.en: So think of it in terms of linearity, right?
cues.zh: 從線性的角度來想，

cues.en: So it looks like, when you go from white to gray, the next step would be black, right?
cues.zh: 白色變成灰色，再下一步就是黑色，對吧？

cues.en: The next step would be black.
cues.zh: 再下一步是黑色。

cues.en: It's a linear progression from bright to dark, and therefore, this is kind of like a linear situation.
cues.zh: 這是由亮到暗的線性漸變，因此可看成一種線性情況。

cues.en: When you take out the black, you break up the linearity.
cues.zh: 去除黑色，就打破了線性。

cues.en: Let's try another one.
cues.zh: 再看另一個。

cues.en: Let's have a look here.
cues.zh: 看看這裡。

cues.en: And at the same time, it's still that same building, right?
cues.zh: 同時，它仍然是原本那棟建築。

cues.en: It's not like you're blending two buildings into each other, but that is secondary.
cues.zh: 並不是把兩棟建築混合在一起，不過這不是重點。

cues.en: The main point is breaking up the linearity.
cues.zh: 重點是打破線性。

cues.en: So let's have a look here. Same thing.
cues.zh: 這裡也是同樣情況。

cues.en: So you see white, gray, black, gray, white.
cues.zh: 可以看到白、灰、黑、灰、白。

cues.en: And when you break it up, you don't have that anymore, right?
cues.zh: 把它打斷後，原本的變化就不見了。

cues.en: You don't have that progression, a gradual progression that you just have like an abrupt change, and that helps introduce non-linearity into your image.
cues.zh: 不再是逐漸變化，而是突然改變，這有助於為影像引入非線性。

cues.en: So it is a very rough explanation, very kind of like on the fingers explanation rather than technical.
cues.zh: 這是很粗略、很直觀的解釋，而非技術性的說明。

cues.en: But hopefully, it kind of helps you understand a bit better what we are talking about here.
cues.zh: 不過希望能幫你更理解我們在談什麼。

cues.en: So here again, you can see white.
cues.zh: 這裡也能看到白色。

cues.en: Gray is a better example even.
cues.zh: 灰色的部分甚至是更好的例子。

cues.en: See bright, darker, darker, darker, darker, darker, darker.
cues.zh: 從亮到暗，再更暗、更暗、更暗、更暗、更暗。

cues.en: So this part looks like it's linear.
cues.zh: 所以這一段看起來是線性的。

cues.en: Then you break it up like that.
cues.zh: 接著像這樣把它打斷。

cues.en: Again, so this is a very rough explanation.
cues.zh: 再次強調，這只是粗略說明。

cues.en: It's not absolutely perfect, but at least it gives you some idea of what's going on.
cues.zh: 不是完全精確，但至少能讓你稍微理解發生了什麼。

cues.en: But if you'd like to learn more, there's a good paper.
cues.zh: 如果想了解更多，有篇不錯的論文。

cues.en: As always, there's always a paper.
cues.zh: 和往常一樣，總有論文可以看。

cues.en: This one is by C.-C. Jay Kuo from the University of California, and it's called "Understanding Convolution Neural Networks Who Have a Mathematical Model."
cues.zh: 這篇由加州大學的 C.-C. Jay Kuo 撰寫，以數學模型理解卷積神經網路為題。

cues.en: And basically, there he answers two questions and you need to just look at the first one, and the question is why a non-linear activation function is essential at the filter output
cues.zh: 文中回答兩個問題，先看第一個就好：為什麼在所有中間層的濾波器輸出端，非線性激活函數

cues.en: of all intermediate layers.
cues.zh: 是不可或缺的？

cues.en: So that kind of explains it in a bit more detail, both in terms of intuition and mostly in terms of mathematics.
cues.zh: 它會從直覺，尤其是數學的角度，更詳細地解釋。

cues.en: So that's an interesting paper where you can get some more additional information on this topic.
cues.zh: 這篇很有意思，能讓你取得這個主題的更多資訊。

cues.en: And if you really want to dig in and explore some cool stuff here, then there's another paper that you might be interested in.
cues.zh: 如果真的想深入探索，還有另一篇你可能會感興趣的論文。

cues.en: It's called "Delving Deep into Rectifiers: Surpassing Human-Level Performance on ImageNet Classification."
cues.zh: 標題是 Delving Deep into Rectifiers: Surpassing Human-Level Performance on ImageNet Classification。

cues.en: And here, the authors, Kaiming He and others, from Microsoft Research, they propose a different type
cues.zh: 微軟研究院的 Kaiming He 等作者，在其中提出不同類型的

cues.en: of rectified linear unit function.
cues.zh: 修正線性單元函數。

cues.en: They propose the parametric rectified linear unit function, which you see here on the right.
cues.zh: 他們提出的是參數化修正線性單元，就是右邊這個。

cues.en: And they argue that it delivers better results with fault sacrificing performance.
cues.zh: 他們主張，它能在不犧牲效能的情況下得到更好的結果。

cues.en: So interesting read if you'd like to get a bit more into this topic.
cues.zh: 如果想再深入一點，這會是有趣的閱讀材料。

cues.en: And that's all for today.
cues.zh: 今天就到這裡。

cues.en: The ReLU layer is pretty simple, pretty safe for just applying the rectifier function.
cues.zh: ReLU 層相當簡單，基本上就是套用整流函數。

cues.en: And I look forward to seeing you next time.
cues.zh: 期待下次與你見面。

cues.en: Until then, enjoy deep learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度學習的樂趣。
